native_result.query: In what context does the gardening pathway for introducing non-native plants show different prevalence styles across habitat types?
native_result.HypoA: The prevalence of gardening-introduced non-native plants differs between urban/cropland habitats and natural habitats.
native_result.HypoB: The gardening pathway shows different prevalence styles according to the intensity and heterogeneity of the surrounding land use, not according to climate. In warm, low-elevation, humid coastal-plain habitats with a heterogeneous, only partly converted matrix (Wetlands and Coastal: ~182 m, 14.6 °C, 645 mm, 22-26% urban and 17-26% cropland cover at 500 m), gardening is the dominant style, supplying the majority of established non-native occurrences (0.56 [0.42-0.69] and 0.54 [0.39-0.68]) at the highest absolute intensity recorded (76-79 gardening occurrences per 100 plots). In habitats governed by a single intensive land use the gardening style is diluted by unintentional contaminant introductions: Croplands (62% cropland at 50 m) falls to 0.19 [0.12-0.27] with 77% unintentional, and the built-up Urban habitat to 0.30 [0.23-0.37] with 69% unintentional - although Urban still receives high absolute gardening propagule input (69 occurrences per 100 plots), so its low share is compositional dilution rather than absence of garden-origin species. Riparian constitutes a third style: intermediate gardening share (0.36 [0.27-0.46], not different from the pooled mean) plus a strong concentration of the AgriForest pathway (13 of 23 occurrences, standardised residual +3.93, MC p=0.0006), i.e. a legacy agro-silvopastoral signature along watercourses. Measured context acts as a modifier in the same direction at both scales - each SD more urban cover reduces the gardening odds by ~27% among habitats (p=0.005) and by ~26% within habitats (p=0.018), cropland cover similarly (p=0.002), and plots with both urban and cropland cover above 15% have a gardening share of 0.245 versus 0.448 where both are below - whereas elevation, rainfall, distance to roads/streams and post-1993 landscape change add nothing once habitat is accounted for. Because habitat labels still improve fit beyond all measured context (quasi-F=7.01, p=5e-06) while context adds only marginally beyond habitat (p=0.12), we hypothesise that the residual differences reflect proximity to the ornamental propagule source (gardens, nurseries, plantings) interacting with habitat, rather than abional conditions: gardening-derived invasion becomes the dominant style in thermally benign, low-lying, structurally open wet/coastal habitats embedded in a mixed low-intensity matrix, and a minority style wherever cropland or dense urban fabric concentrates contaminant propagule pressure. All shares are shares of plot occurrences (plot-level unit), and the apparent gardening excess of the pooled remote seminatural habitats is a denominator artifact (OR 5.34 under invaded-plot denominator vs 0.15 under all-plots denominator) rather than an ecological signal.
native_result.WorkflowB: 1) Inspection (analysis/01_inspection.py): shapes, categorical levels, missingness, duplicate flags; established that invaded_niche_pathways.csv is one row per plot (632 unique coordinates, 0 NAs), that n.total == n.gard+n.unint+n.agfo, and that habitat totals are plot-weighted species occurrences (481 occurrences) rather than species richness; confirmed no crosswalk between the plot file and the 81-species trait file. 2) Data setup (analysis/02_main_analysis.py): success=n.gard, trials=n.total (AgriForest folded into non-gardening); primary frame = 191 invaded plots; sensitivities = all-plots denominator (any plot hosting >=1 gardening species, 632 plots) and AgriForest dropped (n.gard vs n.unint, 396 occurrences); all 10 habitats kept descriptively, five habitats with <=13 occurrences pooled into 'Seminatural-pooled' for confirmatory inference; Clopper-Pearson intervals for shares. 3) Models: quasi-binomial GLM on grouped binomial endog (statsmodels GLM, scale='X2', t-tests) for habitat-only, unpooled 10-level, both sensitivities, context-only, context+habitat, within-habitat (habitat fixed effects), 3-group contrasts, leave-one-habitat-out and leave-one-5km-cell-out refits; home-likelihood beta-binomial MLE (scipy, numerical Hessian SEs) for habitat means, context model and nested comparisons. 4) Permutation inference: Monte-Carlo multinomial G-test (B=20000, fixed row totals and pooled column proportions) on 10x3, 6x3 and 6x2 tables with simulated standardised residuals and per-cell two-sided MC p-values against a Bonferroni threshold, plus a plot-level permutation test in which pathway counts are shuffled across plots (habitat occurrence totals not held fixed). 5) Context characterisation: per-habitat means of elevation, temperature, rainfall, urban and cropland cover at 50 m and 500 m, distance to road/stream, progressive-minus-regressive landscape change, with one variable retained per collinear pair; two-axis style table (composition share vs occurrences per 100 plots); urban and cropland binned shares and a 2x2 cover mosaic; quadratic-term tests for monotonicity. 6) Robustness flagging and exports (results_*.csv, FINDINGS.md). 7) Temporal contingency table used only as one-sentence framing (no habitat key); phylogenetic tree not used (no phylogenetic modelling, per instructions).

sub_hypo.text: Increasing urban and cropland cover reduces gardening prevalence both among and within habitats.
sub_hypo.context: Barcelona province plot-level pathway counts; primary analysis uses 191 invaded plots, with gardening counts as successes and total pathway occurrences as trials. Land cover is characterised within 50 m and 500 m.
